Please read /papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/research-overview/03_FOURTH_ORDER_ARITHMETIC_AND_ACTUAL_PROFILE_PROGRAM_20261020.md, and review the project description in /04_boundary_winding/README.md.
Progress updates are in /04_boundary_winding/research-progress/02_THRESHOLD_SIGNED_ARITHMETIC_PROGRESS_20261020, and chat histories within 04_boundary_winding/chat-histories.

Please summarize the results of the previous research program so that we can brainstorm further about how to proceed.
I’ll read the overview, project description, progress notes, and relevant chat histories, then summarize the results and the questions left open for brainstorming.

The latest round is marked complete. It produced a validated higher-derivative interface and a precise obstruction to the selected profile method, but no new threshold exclusion. I’m checking the underlying notes to distinguish what is reusable from what remains conditional.

The two routes ended differently. The arithmetic route supplied new tools, but its test region already had an event exclusion from lower derivatives. The profile route reached a stronger negative result: even exact theta values at its three sample heights leave room for arbitrarily close neighboring atoms in the relaxation. More precision alone cannot fix that method.

**The latest round produced reusable fourth-order estimation tools and a rigorous failure result for the selected actual-profile method. It did not obtain a new theta event exclusion, an opposing arithmetic sign, or an improved Newman bound.** That is the consistent conclusion of the overview, progress register, underlying notes, and latest research chat.

The central target remains concrete. At a hypothetical ordinary double event,
\[
h_j=\partial_x^jH(T,a),\qquad h_0=h_1=0,\quad h_2\ne0,
\]
the inherited all-real-zero argument gives
\[
S_2=\frac{h_3^2}{9h_2^2}-\frac{h_4}{6h_2}>L,
\]
for an explicitly justified positive \(L\). Consequently,
\[
Q_L=2h_3^2-3h_2h_4-18Lh_2^2>0.
\]
The desired contradiction is an independent, complete arithmetic upper bound \(Q_L\le0\). The necessary-bound theorem already covers every positive height and finite multiplicity, although its double-event form is the current estimating target. [Necessary-bound note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/08_deflated_jet_hierarchy/notes/04_ALL_HEIGHT_MULTIPLICITY_JET_BOUND_20261020.md)

The latest program established three things:

1. **A complete, correlated fourth-order source interface is available on its validation domain.** It encloses physical derivatives through order six, including the sixth derivative needed to control time variation of the fourth. Crucially, it constructs one coherent approximating polynomial and one analytic remainder shared by all derivatives. This makes it possible to preserve correlations that separate derivative bounds discard. The recorded 192- and 256-bit validations passed. [Source-interface note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/notes/02_updated_research_plan/15_COMPLETE_FOURTH_ORDER_INTERFACE_20261020.md)

2. **The event-conditioned optimization has been reduced exactly to one real variable.** Given that complete source approximation and its disk error bound, the Schur construction imposes the exact event cancellations and maximizes the signed fourth-order expression over the permitted residual class. It retains the actual arithmetic center and handles boundary cases.

   However, its theta validation box—near \(T=0.1,\ a=30\)—already satisfies \(|H|>9.07\times10^{-5}\). Thus even \(H=0\) is impossible there. The calculation validates the machinery, but supplies no fourth-order gain on an unresolved event class. A synthetic example demonstrates that correlations can improve a bound; that improvement has not yet been obtained for the physical theta target. [Conditioned-optimizer note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/02_threshold_jet_sign/notes/05_EXACT_EVENT_CONDITIONED_FOURTH_ORDER_SCHUR_CONSUMER_20261020.md)

3. **The selected profile relaxation fails even at exact, actual theta observations.** The experiment used \(D_T(b)=\partial_b\log H(T,ib)\) at \(b=20,40,80\), with \(T=0.1\pm10^{-6}\) and hypothetical event height \(a\in[1001,1002]\).

   After subtracting the hypothetical double pair, those exact observations admit positive relaxed measures containing a unit-count atom arbitrarily close to \(a\). Therefore every count majorant in the selected observation span has objective at least one: it cannot prove the required count \(<1\), hence cannot certify a gap. The same fixed observations permit unbounded relaxed \(S_2\).

   This advances the earlier obstruction from **constructed profile values to specified actual theta values**. Its scope matters: the auxiliary masses need not be integer zero multiplicities, and no physical theta spectrum or entire function is reconstructed. It rules out this three-observation positive-measure relaxation; other schedules and methods retaining additional arithmetic or integer information remain open. [Actual-profile study](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/08_deflated_jet_hierarchy/notes/06_ACTUAL_PROFILE_OBSERVATIONS_AND_RELAXED_DUAL_FAILURE_20261020.md)

The earlier rounds explain why these distinctions matter. Exact Gram correlations improved the selected independent-coordinate bound but left its optimum strictly positive. Adding source positivity and genuine threshold geometry did not repair that estimator: continuous-source controls survived. Earlier finite-profile constructions also concealed nearby-root degeneration, although they did not match actual theta data. These are scoped failures of specified information classes. [Earlier round assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/reviews/01_THRESHOLD_SIGNED_ARITHMETIC_ROUND_REVIEW_20261020.md)

The boundary-winding work also established an explicit forward neighborhood where the proposed later witnesses cannot occur. Any successful later-witness argument must reach beyond that neighborhood through a relation for the unchanged function. Higher-multiplicity machinery is available, but there is still no arithmetic exclusion base case to extend. [Progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/research-progress/02_THRESHOLD_SIGNED_ARITHMETIC_PROGRESS_20261020.md)

For our next brainstorming, I would prioritize:

- **Applying the new arithmetic machinery where it can add information.** Choose a bounded, previously uncovered domain and obtain a complete coupled approximation there. First check event feasibility; then seek a proved improvement in the \(Q_L\) upper bound against the strongest applicable baseline. The high-sector interface still needs its complete complex-disk error estimate.
- **Identifying exactly what additional information could defeat the profile witness.** Integer multiplicities, independently proved local counts or separation, or a justified alternative sample schedule are possible directions. Each needs a quantitative reason it excludes the constructed relaxed measures. More precision on the same three observations cannot help.
- **Revisiting later witnesses only with a concrete nonlocal implication.** Local collision geometry has already been investigated and supplies no contradiction.

The reviews are internal same-model checks with fresh executions of the same programs; they are not specialist review or independently implemented source certificates. The [latest assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/reviews/03_FOURTH_ORDER_AND_ACTUAL_PROFILE_ROUND_REVIEW_20261020.md) preserves those limits.

Why was Q_L chosen again? Please brainstorm further possibilities for the additional information that could defeat the profile witness. Specifically within this project we are looking for topological type arguments that lead to boundary data contradictions. Please place your note in the 04_boundary_winding/brainstorm folder.

I’ll trace why \(Q_L\) became the target, then look for additional information that could exclude the profile witness and support a boundary-data contradiction. I’ll save the brainstorm note in the requested folder, separating established results from proposals.

\(Q_L\) was chosen as an estimate feeding the boundary argument: it encodes a necessary lower bound on deflated curvature without dividing by a potentially tiny \(H_{xx}\). It is not the winding invariant itself. I’m exploring what the profile relaxation discards—integer contour counts, phase information, and consistency across time—and which of those could lead back to a physical boundary contradiction. I’m using the write-page skill for the saved note, following the repository’s format.

There is a concrete topological defect in the displayed profile witness: its three auxiliary masses would give noninteger residues for \(H'/H\), so they cannot be zero multiplicities of a single-valued entire function. Integer contour counts therefore reject that witness, though they do not yet rule out a replacement witness. I’m also developing two routes that fit the project’s boundary focus: counts with wall flux on a spacetime rectangle, and the discriminant of an isolated two-zero group.

The note now includes a more concrete boundary route: certify that a spatial contour contains exactly the double zero, then extract \(S_2\) from a signed harmonic of \(\log|H|\) on that contour. This connects a topological count to the curvature estimate without dividing by the event’s small curvature. I’ve also separated that route from direct spacetime winding, which can bypass \(Q_L\) entirely.

Saved the [brainstorm note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/brainstorm/03_TOPOLOGICAL_BOUNDARY_DATA_AND_PROFILE_WITNESSES_20261020.md), including derivations, control screens, and bounded questions for each proposal.

**\(Q_L\) was chosen because it converts an established necessary curvature bound into a polynomial inequality:**
\[
Q_L=18h_2^2(S_2-L)>0.
\]
It requires derivatives only through order four and avoids division by potentially tiny \(h_2\). Through the critical-value curve, that curvature bound also constrains values on the two time faces.

But **\(Q_L\) is an optional intermediate target**. The original topological contradiction remains
\[
\text{enclosed collision}\ \Longrightarrow\ W_D\le-1,
\qquad
\text{independent arithmetic boundary data}\ \Longrightarrow\ W_D=0.
\]
A successful boundary argument can bypass \(Q_L\) entirely.

There is a concrete distinction available for the profile witness. Its three auxiliary masses require logarithmic-derivative residues approximately
\[
1.143,\qquad 1.944,\qquad 82.523.
\]
I checked that all three remain strictly noninteger throughout the declared parameter domain. They therefore cannot be zero multiplicities of a single-valued entire function: the corresponding contour periods violate the [argument principle](https://dlmf.nist.gov/1.10#E9). This rejects the **displayed witness**, while leaving possible integer replacements unresolved.

The note develops four directions:

- **Physical boundary phase and wall flux.** Retain the cyclic ordering of \((H,H_x)\) around a spacetime boundary, including roots crossing its spatial walls. This directly targets winding zero and handles all finite multiplicities.

- **Integer contour counts and located zeros.** Supplement profile observations with independently certified counts and locations. A contour containing exactly two zeros around the hypothetical double event forbids an additional neighboring zero inside it. This supplies isolation, not yet exclusion.

- **Contour count plus signed boundary modulus.** Once that count establishes a zero-free deflated disk,
  \[
  S_2=-\frac{2}{\pi r^2}\int_0^{2\pi}
  \log|H(T,a+re^{i\theta})|\cos(2\theta)\,d\theta.
  \]
  This gives a specific boundary observation to estimate, with an explicit error allowance, without dividing by the event curvature.

- **The discriminant of an isolated two-zero group.** Spatial contour moments determine \(\Delta=(z_1-z_2)^2\). At an ordinary heat collision, \(\Delta(T)=0\) and \(\Delta'(T)=8\), forcing local complex-time winding one. An independent arithmetic boundary estimate giving winding zero would contradict it.

I recommend prioritizing **direct physical winding with complete wall flux**, with the contour-count/modulus route as a concrete alternative. The saved proposals preserve the requirement that all boundary observations come from the same theta heat flow. Exact diagnostic checks passed; no new theta exclusion is claimed.
Please do an initial investigation of the direct physical winding, and add your results in the notes. Then we can discuss further.

I’ll investigate one bounded direct-winding question, using the existing boundary machinery and controls, and save the result in the investigation’s notes. I’ll focus on what additional boundary information could determine the winding when pointwise interior estimates remain inconclusive.

The earlier winding calculation already succeeded on a covered box, so repeating it would not resolve the missing estimate. I’m examining a more specific possibility: compare the jet directions on the two time faces directly. This could cancel their common rotation and expose the relative phase change that a collision requires, while still accounting for both spatial walls.

The two-face comparison needs an explicit wall condition. I found an exact heat-flow example where the paired face jets have a uniformly positive dot product, yet the boundary winding is −2. All the winding comes from the spatial walls. The example can contain either one fourth-order collision or two ordinary double collisions, so this is a useful test for any proposed certificate.

The calculation now gives a usable formula: physical winding equals the relative winding of the two time faces, plus the left-wall transport, minus the right-wall transport. I also obtained explicit bounds showing that a small neighborhood of an ordinary double event must contain the unfavorable phase crossing. I’m recording both results, the exact controls, and what remains missing for a theta-specific contradiction.

Saved the [initial investigation note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/notes/03_DIRECT_PHYSICAL_WINDING_RELATIVE_PHASE_AND_WALLS_20261020.md), with proofs and replayable exact controls.

Three findings matter:

- **The spatial walls are essential.** Physical winding equals relative winding between the time faces, plus the left-wall transport, minus the right-wall transport.
- **Favorable time faces alone can mislead.** An explicit heat polynomial has a uniformly positive paired-face dot product but winding −2, including an example with two ordinary double collisions.
- **Local Taylor accuracy reinforces the collision.** Explicit error bounds force an antipodal crossing near a double event; shrinking the box cannot supply the opposing winding.

The next substantive target is a coupled theta estimate for the two time faces **and** controlled wall transport. The note specifies the required observations and error bounds. No new theta exclusion was obtained.

This is very promising. I also had the idea of considering a kind of "light cone" type of contour. So you start at the collision at time T=\Lambda. You find some kind of "light cone", which propagates out from that initial collision. Then you cap that contour presumably at infty where perhaps it vanishes or you can bound it. If you can bound that contour integral to be non-integral, then you could argue that there must be a future collision to cancel out the event at T=\Lambda, which would give the desired contradiction (collision at time T=\Lambda implies later collision).

I’ll examine an expanding contour through the exact winding identity, including the cap and the initial collision. A key point to check is whether later collisions could cancel its index: the physical index theorem assigns every collision the same negative sign.
Oh then you'd want to bound the integral in the opposite direction, showing it would have to be a larger negative number

Yes. If the contour encloses the initial double collision and any additional collisions inside it must occur later, then \(W=-1-K_{\mathrm{later}}\). A rigorous bound \(W<-1\) forces \(W\le-2\), hence a later collision. That is the correct direction; I’m checking the contour geometry and cap terms needed to make it valid.

The quadratic control gives a useful test of the cap idea. For a cone wider than the natural \(\sqrt{2(t-T)}\) splitting, the cap retains the original winding as it recedes. For a narrower cone, the cap contribution tends to zero, but the walls retain the winding. So a vanishing cap can help, but the remaining boundary estimate must be strictly more negative than the initial event’s contribution.

There is also a way to make the cone start at the collision itself. For an ordinary double event, dividing \(H+iH_x\) by its invertible linearization removes the initial singularity: the quotient extends continuously to value \(1\) at the event. Negative winding of that quotient on a capped forward cone would then count only later collisions. I’m saving this formulation with the cap calculation.

Exactly. For a complete contour enclosing the initial ordinary double collision, with every other enclosed collision occurring later,
\[
W(\Gamma_R)=-1-K_{\mathrm{later}}.
\]
Therefore **a rigorous bound \(W(\Gamma_R)<-1\) forces a later collision**. That contradicts \(T=\Lambda\), because a later multiple zero would have nonreal predecessors still above \(T\). [Polymath, §3](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.12438v2#S3)

Your cone can be made precise. A square-root opening is natural because the newborn roots move initially like \(a\pm\sqrt{2(t-T)}\). The singular apex can either be enclosed in a small neighborhood or removed by dividing the physical jet by its linearization. That quotient extends continuously to \(1\) at the initial double event; its negative winding on a forward cone would count only later collisions.

The cap calculation identifies the missing estimate. For the exact quadratic control:

- A wide expanding cone leaves the original \(-2\pi\) phase on the distant cap.
- A narrow cone has cap contribution tending to zero, while its walls retain \(-2\pi\).

So **cap decay alone is insufficient; we need a signed bound strictly beyond the initial contribution**, including both walls. A finite cap already suffices. For initial multiplicity \(m\), replace \(1\) by \(\lfloor m/2\rfloor\).

I saved the derivations and apex regularization in the [expanding-contour note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/notes/04_EXPANDING_CONTOURS_AND_A_LATER_COLLISION_TARGET_20261020.md). The theta-specific boundary estimate remains open.

Can you create a research program around this idea? Maybe it merits a new folder within threshhold_routes? If so, can you create that folder, and write the research overview and research progress files there?

I’ll make this a separate threshold route, with a research overview and progress register. I’ll center it on the corrected target—forcing winding below the initial event’s contribution—and make the apex, wall transport, cap bounds, and collision controls explicit parts of the program.

This merits a ninth route because it gives the later-collision idea a concrete contour and estimate to study. I’m keeping the first goal finite: bound the complete contour’s winding below the initial collision’s contribution. The cap at infinity will be an optional extension, since the existing quadratic control shows that a vanishing cap can still leave exactly the original collision’s winding on the walls.

The program now has three concrete lines of attack: estimate the phase after removing the initial collision’s index; track root transport across moving walls; and test whether walls that follow simple roots make the cap estimate easier. Each must reach beyond the already-proved local region with no later collisions. I’m making the first research milestone a precise contour and source-data contract, followed by one bounded attempt at the signed estimate.

The overview and progress register are drafted. They distinguish the inherited results from work still to do, define the strict winding margin, and include controls that catch lost wall transport or miscounted initial multiplicity. I’m checking the formulas, links and parent indexes before saving the route.

Created **BW-09: Expanding contours and later collisions** under `threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision`.

- [Research overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/research-overview/01_EXPANDING_CONTOUR_RESEARCH_PROGRAM_20261020.md)
- [Research progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/research-progress/01_EXPANDING_CONTOUR_PROGRESS_20261020.md)

The program targets winding **strictly below the initial collision’s contribution**, with explicit apex, moving-wall and cap estimates. It starts with finite contours and includes root-following walls as an alternative; infinite caps and higher multiplicities are later extensions.

The progress file separates inherited results from unstarted tasks. I also updated the parent indexes and checked the links. The first research task is to select one contour and specify the theta estimate needed to produce the extra negative winding.
